# Executive Summary

# Data and Exploratory Data Analysis
- Use the tidy data from part 1
- Create hydrographs for the extreme events
- Observations of the hydrographs and understand the variety in flood event shapes

# Statistical methodology
- fitting each of the statistical methods; The Polynomial regression, PCA, Wavelets
- uncertainty modelling for each method

# Results and validation
- Compare the different methods 
- Examine residual plots to investigate whether the method performs poorly on unusual flood events
- e.g do testing and training data to assess how well the methods peform

# Recommendation
- Recommend the best method and justify
- explain the limitations and uncertainity with each method

# Emulator application
- Give a brief explanation of how the emulator would be used
- e.g, explain the two seperate phases,
  
First, SEPA could select different parameter combinations, reconstruct corresponding hydrographs and run these through the actual flood inundation model. The resulting input-output pairs would be used to train an emulator.

Second, SEPA could repeatedly sample parameters from your fitted uncertainty distribution and feed those parameters into the trained emulator to obtain a distribution of predicted flood outcomes.

# Conclusion
